description: Explicit instruction to ignore or disregard prior instructions/system prompt.
falsePositiveNotes: Legitimate users occasionally ask an assistant to 'ignore the previous answer' in normal conversation repair -- distinguish by checking whether the phrase targets 'instructions/rules/system' vs. 'answer/response'.

description: Instruction telling the model to disregard its safety guidelines or content policy.
falsePositiveNotes: Security researchers and red-teamers legitimately discuss 'guidelines' in meta-conversation; check context before blocking.

description: Retrieved/third-party content directly addresses 'the AI' or 'assistant' rather than a human reader.
falsePositiveNotes: Rare in genuine documents; some AI-safety blog posts and papers legitimately address 'the AI' in examples -- these should self-identify via source allow-listing.

description: Alt-text or title attribute containing instruction-shaped language rather than a genuine image description.
falsePositiveNotes: Some legitimate alt text mentions 'system' (e.g. 'system diagram') -- combine with instruction verbs to reduce noise.

description: Tool/function description contains an embedded instruction directing the model to take an additional undisclosed action or exfiltrate data.
falsePositiveNotes: Legitimate tool docs sometimes describe genuine side effects ('also logs to audit trail') -- verify the destination is your own sanctioned logging path, not an external one.

description: Tool output contains what looks like a new tool-call directive, suggesting a compromised or malicious tool result attempting to chain further actions.
falsePositiveNotes: Legitimate multi-step tool outputs (e.g. a planner tool describing next steps) can resemble this; only elevate to block when the referenced function is a real, more-privileged tool in your registry.

description: Unusually long or high-cardinality DNS subdomain label pattern, consistent with DNS-based exfiltration.
falsePositiveNotes: Some legitimate CDNs and cloud storage services use long hashed subdomains; allow-list your known providers (e.g. *.s3.amazonaws.com, *.cloudfront.net).

description: Request for 'everything above/before this point' framed to extract hidden context.
falsePositiveNotes: Occasionally used legitimately in document QA ('summarize everything above') -- distinguish 'summarize' from 'repeat verbatim'.

description: High-density run of base64-alphabet characters, consistent with an encoded payload smuggled inside otherwise plain text.
falsePositiveNotes: Legitimate content legitimately includes base64 (image data URIs, JWTs, signed tokens); only actionable combined with a suspicious surrounding context or decoded content.

description: Classic 'DAN' / 'Do Anything Now' or equivalent named unrestricted-persona jailbreak framing.
falsePositiveNotes: These named jailbreak personas have essentially no legitimate use; safe to block, though keep the list of named personas updated as new ones circulate.
